content: Before using this medication, visually inspect the product for any particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Common side effects of this medication may include drowsiness, dizziness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, or headache. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance regarding side effects. Before using hydroxyzine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to cetirizine, to levocetirizine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Hydroxyzine may also cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase your risk of QT prolongation, especially if you are using certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, particularly drowsiness, confusion, constipation, difficulty urinating, or QT prolongation. Children may also be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications (such as allergy or cough-and-cold products) because they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (such as allergy skin tests or urine corticosteroid tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Important Note: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
